- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer or adjust downward early in forecast horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply decay or tapering to forecast slope post-spike.
- Model shows strong upward bias in early forecast days (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; apply mean reversion or downward adjustment if sentiment stabilizes or turns neutral.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast at day 1–3, consider sentiment-driven correction: if sentiment drops, reduce forecast; if sentiment rises, increase but cap growth.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price moves faster than model; adjust for recent sentiment momentum — e.g., if sentiment is trending up, forecast should accelerate toward true path.
- When sentiment history shows repeated peaks followed by corrections, model tends to overcorrect; apply smoothing or dampen forecast curvature after peak days.
